To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) language modeling is a strong pretraining objective, (2) it can be improved with additional objectives, and (3) there is still a lot of room for improvement.

(1) language modeling is the most effective pretraining task for the majority of tasks, (2) pretraining and freezing is the least effective pretraining strategy, (3) pretraining is most effective when it is used to initialize a model that will be finetuned for the downstream task, and (4) the best results are obtained when pretraining and finetuning are combined in a single training procedure

(1) language modeling is a good pretraining task for contextualized word representations; (2) the best language modeling pretraining is done on large corpora; and (3) the pretraining task is not the only factor in determining performance, and the choice of architecture and the amount of data used for pretraining are also important.

we need to better understand the role of pretraining and how to best use pretrained sentence encoders, and we need to develop better ways to compare models in the sentence-level context.
